title: Arithmetic Λ-rings, relative q-Witt vectors and complete framed calculus
summary: Build the general big Witt and arithmetic Λ library, absolute and relative q-Witt rings, completed étale coefficient Frobenius, positive-degree systems and complete framed difference calculus, culminating in smooth torsion and completion theorems. Export the functorial p-complete E∞ de Rham comparison for all smooth algebras, primes and positive indices.

layers.title: Big Witt rings and shared homological algebra

targets.name: BigWitt.TruncationSet
targets.statement: A truncation set S is a subset of positive integers closed under positive divisors, including the empty set. Put S/n = {e > 0 | ne ∈ S}, Div(m) = {d > 0 | d divides m}, and w_n(x) = ∑_{d|n} d x_d^(n/d) for x ∈ R^S and n ∈ S.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring, possibly without identity

locator.where: §1 before Proposition 1.2, lines 217–268; Wagner §2.6, wagner line 435; printed hesselholt v3 pp. 6–7; wagner v5 p. 10

api.name: TruncationSet.ext
api.statement: Equality is membership equivalence.

api.name: TruncationSet.div_mem
api.statement: S/n is divisor closed; (S/n)/k = S/(nk).

api.name: BigWitt.ghostPolynomial_map
api.statement: w_n commutes with every coefficient ring map.

api.name: TruncationSet.mk
api.statement: A subset of positive integers and a proof of divisor closure construct a truncation set; Div(m) is the canonical finite example.

tests.name: BigWitt.TruncationSet_1
tests.statement: For Div(6), w_6 = x_1^6 + 2x_2^3 + 3x_3^2 + 6x_6; omission of mixed prime divisors fails.

tests.name: BigWitt.TruncationSet_2
tests.statement: The empty set gives the singleton product and no ghost coordinates.

tests.name: BigWitt.TruncationSet_3
tests.statement: w_1 = x_1, w_2 = x_1^2 + 2x_2; using zero-based p-typical indices fails. The subset {2} is not a truncation set because it omits 1.

targets.proofSketch: Finite divisor sums define integral polynomials; divisor transitivity gives the closure and evaluation laws.

targets.name: BigWitt.ghost_image
targets.statement: If B has endomorphisms φ_p lifting pth powers modulo p, a sequence b ∈ B^S lies in the ghost image iff b_n ≡ φ_p(b_{n/p}) modulo p^v_p(n)B for every n ∈ S and prime p dividing n. Ghosts are injective if multiplication by every n ∈ S is injective on B. The injectivity assertion holds for every commutative B without specifying Frobenius lifts.
hypotheses: B is a commutative unital ring; a lift φ_p is specified for every prime appearing in S. Pairwise commutation is unnecessary for the ghost image criterion.

locator.where: Lemma 1.1, lines 217–267; Lemma 1.9; printed hesselholt v3 pp. 6–7, 11

api.name: BigWitt.ghost_injective
api.statement: Integer torsion-freeness at all primes occurring in S implies ghost injectivity.

api.name: BigWitt.ghost_equiv_of_units
api.statement: If all n ∈ S are units, the ghost map is bijective.

tests.name: BigWitt.ghost_image_1
tests.statement: Over ℤ with φ_2 = id and S = Div(2), b_2 ≡ b_1 modulo 2 is the image condition.

tests.name: BigWitt.ghost_image_2
tests.statement: Over 𝔽₂, (0,1) has both ghost coordinates zero for S = Div(2); injectivity without torsion-freeness fails.

tests.name: BigWitt.ghost_image_3
tests.statement: For S = ∅, the empty sequence is in the image and the map is injective.

targets.proofSketch: Choose Witt coordinates in divisor order; the congruences make the next numerator divisible by n. Uniqueness needs n-torsion-freeness, existence does not require dividing by a unit.

targets.name: BigWitt
targets.statement: Construct the natural commutative ring W_S(R) on R^S whose ghost polynomials are ring maps. For nonunital R use the same integral operation polynomials. For T ⊆ S, restriction is a ring map; W_S is the inverse limit of its finite subtruncations.
hypotheses: S is any truncation set; R is commutative, with or without identity.

locator.where: Proposition 1.2, lines 268–298; Proposition 1.6 proof, lines 383–397; wagner §2.6; printed hesselholt v3 pp. 7, 10; wagner v5 pp. 10–11

api.name: BigWitt.mk_coeff
api.statement: Coordinates construct every element; coeff (mk x) d = x_d.

api.name: BigWitt.ext
api.statement: Elements agree iff all their Witt coordinates agree.

api.name: BigWitt.map
api.statement: Ring maps act on coordinates; map_id and map_comp hold.

api.name: BigWitt.restrict_comp
api.statement: Restrictions compose and commute with ghosts and coefficient maps.

api.name: BigWitt.nonunital_unitization
api.statement: W_S(R) identifies with the kernel for W_S(ℤ ⋉ R) → W_S(ℤ).

tests.name: BigWitt_1
tests.statement: In W_Div(2)(ℤ), τ(1)+τ(1) has coordinates (2,−1), not (2,0).

tests.name: BigWitt_2
tests.statement: W_∅(R) and W_S(0) are zero rings; W_{1}(R) ≅ R.

tests.name: BigWitt_3
tests.statement: For the nonunital ring R=(ℤ,+) with zero multiplication, W_Div(2)(R) has componentwise addition and zero multiplication: (a,b)+(c,d)=(a+c,b+d) and (a,b)(c,d)=(0,0). A spurious unit in R would change these operations.

targets.proofSketch: Apply 1.2 over the torsion-free polynomial ring in universal coordinates to obtain integral addition, multiplication and negatives. Verify identities there by ghosts and specialize. The kernel model handles nonunital inputs without a fictitious unit.

targets.name: BigWitt.frobenius
targets.statement: For every n > 0 construct F_n : W_S(R) → W_{S/n}(R), additive V_n in the reverse direction, and the multiplicative Teichmüller map τ : R → W_S(R). Ghosts satisfy w_e F_n = w_{ne}; (V_n x)_{ne} = x_e and other coordinates vanish.
hypotheses: S is divisor closed; R is a commutative ring; units are preserved in the unital case.

locator.where: Lemmas 1.3–1.5, lines 301–371; printed hesselholt v3 pp. 8–9

api.name: BigWitt.frobenius_comp
api.statement: F_a F_b = F_{ab}; V_a V_b = V_{ab} with the indicated shifted truncations.

api.name: BigWitt.frobenius_verschiebung
api.statement: On W_{S/n}(R), F_n V_n = n.

api.name: BigWitt.frobenius_verschiebung_gcd
api.statement: For c = gcd(a,b), F_a V_b = c V_{b/c} F_{a/c} on W_{S/b}(R), with target W_{S/a}(R).

api.name: BigWitt.projection_formula
api.statement: x V_n(y) = V_n(F_n(x)y).

api.name: BigWitt.teichmuller_ghost
api.statement: w_e(τ(r)) = r^e and F_n τ(r) = τ(r)^n.

api.name: BigWitt.verschiebung_teichmuller_expansion
api.statement: x = ∑_{d∈S} V_d τ(x_d), converging in the finite-restriction topology.

tests.name: BigWitt.frobenius_2
tests.statement: F_1 and V_1 are identities, including S=∅.

tests.name: BigWitt.frobenius_3
tests.statement: τ(−1) = −τ(1)+V_2τ(1) in W_Div(2)(ℤ); treating τ as additive fails.

targets.proofSketch: Construct F by the universal polynomial argument in 1.2; define V and τ on coordinates. Prove all identities on universal torsion-free rings using ghosts, then specialize.

targets.name: BigWitt.pTypicalEquiv
targets.statement: For prime p and a ≥ 0, coordinate reindexing d=p^i gives W_Div(p^a)(R) ≃+* TruncatedWittVector p (a+1) R; the infinite p-power truncation gives WittVector p R. These equivalences preserve ghosts, τ, V and F with their shifted lengths.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; p is prime.

locator.where: Remark 2.7, lines 471–473; printed wagner v5 p. 11

api.name: BigWitt.pTypicalEquiv_coeff
api.statement: Coefficient p^i corresponds to coefficient i.

api.name: BigWitt.pTypicalEquiv_truncate
api.statement: Big restrictions correspond to TruncatedWittVector.truncate.

tests.name: BigWitt.pTypicalEquiv_1
tests.statement: W_Div(1)(R) has length 1 for every p; length 0 is the zero ring.

tests.name: BigWitt.pTypicalEquiv_2
tests.statement: At p=2,a=1 the second ghost is x_0^2+2x_1 on both carriers.

tests.name: BigWitt.pTypicalEquiv_3
tests.statement: At p=3,a=2 the final ghost is x_0^9+3x_1^3+9x_2.

targets.proofSketch: The ghost polynomials agree after reindexing; compare operation polynomials over ℤ and transport. Infinite sequences follow by compatible finite restrictions.

targets.name: BigWitt.etale_baseChange
targets.statement: For an étale map R → R′, a finite truncation set S and n > 0, W_S(R) → W_S(R′) is étale and W_S(R′) ⊗_{W_S(R),F_n} W_{S/n}(R) ≅ W_{S/n}(R′). For coprime positive a,b there is a natural W_Div(ab)(R) ≅ W_Div(a)(W_Div(b)(R)).
hypotheses: R and R′ are commutative unital rings; S is finite in the étale assertion.

locator.where: Theorem 1.25, lines 811–827; borger Corollary 5.4, borger line 1323; printed hesselholt v3 p. 19; borger v6 p. 26

api.name: BigWitt.etale_baseChange_natural
api.statement: The tensor comparison is induced by F_n and the coefficient map, natural in étale squares.

tests.name: BigWitt.etale_baseChange_1
tests.statement: S=∅ gives the unique map of zero rings and a zero tensor product.

tests.name: BigWitt.etale_baseChange_2
tests.statement: S={1} recovers the original étale map.

tests.name: BigWitt.etale_baseChange_3
tests.statement: The theorem has finite S: no finite-presentation conclusion is inferred for the infinite big Witt functor.

targets.proofSketch: Use prime-set decomposition and the finite p-typical étale lifting argument, reducing the Frobenius square modulo p by relative Frobenius for étale algebras. Iterate and use finite divisor induction as in Hesselholt 1.25.

targets.name: CommutingEndomorphisms.koszulComplex
targets.statement: For a commutative ring B, a B-module M and r commuting B-linear endomorphisms D_i, define the cochain complex K(M;D)^k = M⊗_B ∧^k B^r, with differential d(m⊗e_I)=∑_i D_i(m)⊗e_i∧e_I. Give endomorphism-compatible maps, signed coordinate permutations, direct sums, arbitrary scalar extension and cohomology base change for flat scalar extensions, concatenation by iterated two-term totalization, and the comparison with the supplied scalar Koszul complex.
hypotheses: r≥0; M any B-module; D_iD_j=D_jD_i; B any commutative ring.

locator.where: Remark 2.16, lines 603–619; §4.7, lines 2847–2857; printed wagner v5 pp. 13–14, 57

api.name: commutingEndomorphismKoszul_d_sq
api.statement: Commutativity of the D_i implies d²=0, with no regularity assumption.

api.name: commutingEndomorphismKoszul_map
api.statement: A map intertwining every D_i induces a chain map; identities and composition hold.

api.name: commutingEndomorphismKoszul_ext
api.statement: Maps induced by intertwining maps are determined in degree zero.

api.name: commutingEndomorphismKoszul_scalar
api.statement: For M=B and D_i multiplication by f_i, identify this complex with the cochain dual of the supplied chain scalar Koszul model, using the coordinate dual bases.

tests.name: QWitt.commutingEndomorphismKoszul_1
tests.statement: For r=2, d⁰(m)=(D₁m,D₂m) and d¹(a,b)=D₁b−D₂a; using a plus in both positions fails d²=0.

tests.name: QWitt.commutingEndomorphismKoszul_2
tests.statement: For r=0 the complex is M in degree zero; for M=0 it vanishes.

tests.name: QWitt.commutingEndomorphismKoszul_3
tests.statement: On M=ℤ² with basis u₁,u₂, take D₁(u₁)=0, D₁(u₂)=u₁, D₂(u₁)=u₂, D₂(u₂)=0. Then d²(u₁)=u₁⊗(e₁∧e₂)≠0; omitting commutativity of the endomorphisms would not give a complex.

targets.proofSketch: Give M its B[X_i]-module structure with X_i acting by D_i. Tensor with the supplied finite scalar Koszul resolution, using the cochain wedge convention, and compare termwise. This is the module-action bridge to the supplier complex, not a second scalar Koszul construction.

targets.name: QWitt.arithmeticFracture
targets.statement: For M in the enhanced derived category of ℤ-modules and any positive integer N, the square M→∏_{p|N}M^∧_p, M[1/N]→∏_{p|N}M^∧_p[1/p] is a pullback. Localization at N and p-completion for p|N jointly detect zero objects. Rationalization and all prime completions jointly detect zero objects.
hypotheses: N>0; M arbitrary, possibly unbounded; each product indexed by p|N is finite.

locator.where: Lemma 2.4, Remark 2.5, lines 366–430; §4.18, lines 3081–3095; printed wagner v5 pp. 9–10, 62

api.name: arithmeticFracture_natural
api.statement: The pullback is natural in M and compatible with coefficient algebra objects.

tests.name: QWitt.arithmeticFracture_1
tests.statement: For N=1 the right product is zero and the left vertical map is identity.

tests.name: QWitt.arithmeticFracture_2
tests.statement: For M=ℤ,N=2 the square is ℤ→ℤ₂ over ℤ[1/2]→ℚ₂.

tests.name: QWitt.arithmeticFracture_3
tests.statement: p-completion alone kills ℤ[1/p]; joint detection needs the localization term.

targets.proofSketch: Apply localization and each indicated completion to the fibre of the proposed square; the resulting squares split. Prove conservativity first from derived completeness as RHom of the localization cone, then pass over all N for rational detection.

layers.examples: Divisors of 1, 2, 6 and prime powers distinguish the big indexing from p-typical length.

layers.title: Arithmetic Λ-rings, prime sets and perfection

targets.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing
targets.statement: Give the full big Witt functor W = W_{positive integers} its comonad structure Δ : W(R) → W(W(R)), counit w_1, characterized by w_n Δ = F_n. An arithmetic Λ-ring is a commutative unital ring A with a ring coaction s : A → W(A) satisfying w_1 s = id and Δs = W(s)s. Define Λ-maps by coaction compatibility and ψ_n = w_n s.
hypotheses: A is a commutative unital ring, with torsion allowed.

locator.where: Proposition 1.19 and Definitions 1.21, 1.23, lines 711–801; printed hesselholt v3 pp. 17–19

api.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.mk
api.statement: A coaction and its two coalgebra equations construct the structure.

api.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.hom_ext
api.statement: Λ-maps are equal when their underlying ring maps are equal.

api.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.adams_one_mul
api.statement: ψ_1=id and ψ_a ψ_b=ψ_{ab}.

api.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.adams_prime_mod
api.statement: ψ_p(a)−a^p belongs to pA for every prime p.

api.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.ofFrobeniusLifts
api.statement: On ℤ-torsion-free A, commuting prime Frobenius lifts determine a unique Λ-structure.

api.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.adams_isLambdaHom
api.statement: Each ψ_n commutes with the coaction and defines a Λ-endomorphism.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing_1
tests.statement: The canonical structure on ℤ has ψ_n(k)=k, including ψ_2(2)=2, not 4.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing_2
tests.statement: The toric structure has ψ_2(T)=T² and ψ_3(T)=T³.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing_3
tests.statement: Commuting identity Adams maps on 𝔽₂ do not define an arithmetic Λ-ring: the p-coordinate δ_2(2)=−1 contradicts 2=0. Adams congruences alone lose torsion data.

targets.proofSketch: Construct Δ by 1.2 on universal coordinates and prove coalgebra laws by ghosts. The coaction equations imply Adams laws. The torsion-free converse is the same ghost congruence criterion, not a definition on torsion rings.

targets.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.primeSet
targets.statement: For any set P of primes construct the P-typical Witt comonad and its Λ_P-coalgebras; on P-torsion-free rings these are commuting ψ_p with ψ_p(x) ≡ x^p modulo p. Give change-of-prime-set functors, free Λ_P-rings on sets, and reflexive presentations by free Λ_P-rings. Finite Div(m) q-Witt data require only P={p | p divides m}.
hypotheses: P is arbitrary; coalgebras, rather than Adams-only structures, are used on rings with torsion.

locator.where: §§1.16–1.18, lines 603–638; pridham Definition 2.1, pridham line 506; wagner Remarks 2.32 and 2.43; printed borger v6 pp. 12–13; pridham v4 p. 12; wagner v5 pp. 26, 31

api.name: LambdaP.restrict
api.statement: For P′⊆P restrict the operations and coaction.

api.name: LambdaP.free_homEquiv
api.statement: Λ_P-maps from the free ring on I to A correspond naturally to I → A.

api.name: LambdaP.hom_ext
api.statement: Maps from the free ring agree when they agree on its generators.

api.name: LambdaP.singlePrime_wittCoalgebra
api.statement: For P={p}, identify the coaction with the usual p-typical Witt-coalgebra notion of δ-ring.

api.name: LambdaP.free_polynomial
api.statement: The free Λ-ring on I has underlying polynomial ring on the universal exterior operations of its generators; Adams operations have faithfully flat underlying maps.

api.name: LambdaP.filteredColimit
api.statement: Filtered colimits are created on underlying rings: every coordinate operation and every defining relation uses finitely many arguments.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.primeSet_1
tests.statement: P=∅ gives ordinary commutative rings and the identity Witt comonad.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.primeSet_2
tests.statement: P={2} uses infinite 2-typical Witt vectors, not length two.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.primeSet_3
tests.statement: The free Λ-ring on no generators is ℤ, with all Adams operations identity.

targets.proofSketch: Restrict Witt indices to the monoid generated by P; repeat the comonad construction. The free object is represented by symmetric-operation generators and the coalgebra equations. Its polynomial presentation supplies the reflexive coequalizer and faithful-flat Adams property needed in 2.4. The faithful-flat statement uses the free polynomial presentation and prime-set decomposition; it does not identify an Adams operation with a literal permutation of the exterior-operation generators.

targets.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.perfection
targets.statement: Call A perfect if every ψ_n, n>0, is an isomorphism. Construct A^perf as the filtered colimit of A indexed by positive integers under divisibility, with transition A_m → A_n equal to ψ_{n/m}. The resulting Λ-map A → A^perf is initial among Λ-maps to perfect Λ-rings.
hypotheses: A is an arithmetic Λ-ring; colimits are in commutative Λ-rings.

locator.where: Remark 2.47 and footnote 2.3, lines 1621–1643; bhatt-scholze Remark 2.27, bhatt-scholze line 775; printed wagner v5 p. 32; bhatt-scholze v4 p. 20

api.name: LambdaPerfection.lift
api.statement: Maps to a perfect B extend uniquely and naturally across A → A^perf.

api.name: LambdaPerfection.adamsEquiv
api.statement: Every Adams operation on A^perf has its shift inverse.

api.name: LambdaPerfection.idempotent
api.statement: If A is perfect then A → A^perf is an isomorphism.

api.name: LambdaPerfection.map
api.statement: Λ-maps induce maps of perfections with identity and composition laws.

api.name: LambdaPerfection.of
api.statement: The stage-one map sends a to its colimit class; at stages m|n the class of a equals the class of ψ_{n/m}(a).

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.perfection_1
tests.statement: ℤ^perf=ℤ; replacing arithmetic perfection by characteristic-p perfection fails.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.perfection_2
tests.statement: For toric ℤ[T], the perfection is ℤ[T^r | r is a nonnegative rational], with ψ_n(T^r)=T^(nr).

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.perfection_3
tests.statement: T has no preimage under ψ_2 on ℤ[T]; ℤ[T] itself is not perfect.

targets.proofSketch: Adams operations commute with the coaction, so form the directed colimit. Index shifts invert each ψ_n. The universal map sends a at stage m to ψ_m^{-1}(f(a)).

targets.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.IsPerfectlyCovered
targets.statement: A is perfectly covered if there exists a faithfully flat Λ-map A → B with B perfect. This is equivalent to every ψ_n being faithfully flat, and to A → A^perf being faithfully flat. Such A is ℤ-torsion-free; so are its flat algebras.
hypotheses: A is an arithmetic Λ-ring; the zero ring is allowed under the usual faithful-flat convention.

locator.where: Remark 2.47 and footnote 2.3, lines 1621–1643; wagner-habiro §1.22(e), wagner-habiro line 493; bhatt-scholze Lemma 2.28, bhatt-scholze line 778; printed wagner v5 p. 32; wagner-habiro v2 p. 12; bhatt-scholze v4 p. 20

api.name: IsPerfectlyCovered.iff_adams
api.statement: The three conditions in the statement are equivalent.

api.name: IsPerfectlyCovered.torsionFree
api.statement: Multiplication by every positive integer is injective on A.

api.name: IsPerfectlyCovered.polynomial
api.statement: Toric polynomial algebras over a perfectly covered Λ-base are perfectly covered, for any variable set.

api.name: IsPerfectlyCovered.free
api.statement: Every free arithmetic Λ-ring on a set is perfectly covered.

api.name: IsPerfectlyCovered.mk
api.statement: A perfect Λ-ring B and a faithfully flat Λ-map A→B give a witness of perfect coverage.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.IsPerfectlyCovered_1
tests.statement: On ℤ[T], ψ_2 is finite free with basis 1,T and ψ_3 with basis 1,T,T².

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.IsPerfectlyCovered_2
tests.statement: ℤ, every perfect Λ-ring and the free ring on the empty set satisfy the predicate.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaRing.IsPerfectlyCovered_3
tests.statement: For A=ℤ[ε]/(ε²) with ψ_n(ε)=nε, the torsion-free Frobenius-lift criterion gives a Λ-ring, but ψ_2 is not flat: after reduction modulo 2, ε acts by zero on the nonzero target dual-number ring. Thus A is not perfectly covered, and torsion-freeness alone is insufficient.

targets.proofSketch: Use faithful-flat descent on the ψ_n-twisted tensor functors and filtered colimits of faithful-flat maps. The p-coordinate of a coaction gives px=0 ⇒ ψ_p(x)=0 as in the δ torsion lemma; injective Adams on the cover kill p-torsion, and faithful flatness descends this conclusion. Polynomial monomial bases and 2.2 prove the examples.

targets.name: ArithmeticLambdaAlgebra.IsRelativelyPerfect
targets.statement: For any A-algebra R define the twist R^(n)=R⊗_{A,ψ_n}A with its right-hand A-algebra structure. If R is a Λ-A-algebra, define relative perfection by invertibility of ψ_{p/A}:R^(p)→R, r⊗a↦ψ_p(r)a, for every prime p; equivalently these maps are invertible for every positive n.
hypotheses: A is an arithmetic Λ-ring and R any commutative unital A-algebra; linearized Adams maps and relative perfection additionally require a compatible Λ-structure on R.

locator.where: §2.45 and Remark 2.47, lines 1573–1628; printed wagner v5 pp. 31–32

api.name: LambdaAlgebra.linearizedAdams_tmul
api.statement: ψ_{n/A}(r⊗a)=ψ_n(r)a; tensor balancing uses ψ_n on A.

api.name: LambdaAlgebra.twist_comp
api.statement: (R^(a))^(b) ≅ R^(ab), naturally and compatibly with linearized Adams.

api.name: IsRelativelyPerfect.ofPerfect
api.statement: If A and R are perfect Λ-rings and A → R is a Λ-map, then R is relatively perfect.

api.name: LambdaAlgebra.twist_hom_ext
api.statement: A-algebra maps out of the twist are determined on pure tensors.

api.name: IsRelativelyPerfect.ofPrimeEquivalences
api.statement: A compatible Λ-A-algebra and equivalences for every ψ_{p/A} give relative perfection; these equivalences respect the fixed linearized maps.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaAlgebra.IsRelativelyPerfect_1
tests.statement: For R=A the linearized map is an isomorphism even when ψ_p on A is not surjective.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaAlgebra.IsRelativelyPerfect_2
tests.statement: ℤ[T] over ℤ is not relatively perfect: T is outside the image of linearized ψ_2.

tests.name: ArithmeticLambdaAlgebra.IsRelativelyPerfect_3
tests.statement: For A=ℤ and perfect R the definition reduces to invertibility of ψ_p on R.

targets.proofSketch: The tensor balancing relation is ψ_n-compatible because A → R is a Λ-map. Associativity of scalar extension proves the composite law, and prime factorization reduces all n to primes.

layers.examples: The toric ring ℤ[T] is perfectly covered but not perfect; ℤ is perfect. Characteristic-p perfection is a different object.

layers.title: Absolute q-Witt rings and exactness

targets.name: QWitt.AbsoluteFVSystem
targets.statement: For a commutative ring R define a q-FV system to consist of Z[q]-rings E_m, m>0, structural maps W_Div(m)(R)[q]/(q^m−1) → E_m, Z[q]-linear additive V_{m/d}:E_d → E_m and multiplicative Z[q]-algebra maps F_{m/d}:E_m → E_d compatible with the ordinary Witt maps, and satisfying FV=m/d and VF=[m/d]_{q^d}. The unital variant preserves units; the nonunital variant uses nonunital rings with Z[q]-action. Morphisms preserve every structure map.
hypotheses: R may be nonunital; d divides m and d,m>0.

locator.where: Definition 2.8 and Remark 2.12, lines 475–549; printed wagner v5 pp. 11–12

api.name: AbsoluteFVSystem.mk
api.statement: Compatible structural, F and V maps with the two composite laws give a system.

api.name: AbsoluteFVSystem.hom_ext
api.statement: A morphism is determined by its maps on E_m.

api.name: AbsoluteFVSystem.truncate
api.statement: Restrict the system to any divisor-closed set of positive indices.

tests.name: QWitt.AbsoluteFVSystem_1
tests.statement: For R=ℤ, E_m=ℤ[q]/(q^m−1), F is reduction and V is multiplication by [m/d]_{q^d}.

tests.name: QWitt.AbsoluteFVSystem_2
tests.statement: The zero nonunital ring gives the zero system.

tests.name: QWitt.AbsoluteFVSystem_3
tests.statement: Using V_2=2 in the ℤ example fails VF=1+q at m=2.

targets.proofSketch: Specify the category with all structural commutative squares. The polynomial model for ℤ verifies that the two composite laws impose distinct requirements.

targets.name: QWitt.absolute
targets.statement: Construct the initial q-FV system Q_m(R). It is W_Div(m)(R)[q]/I_m, where I_m is generated by (q^d−1)V_{m/d}(x) and [d/e]_{q^e}V_{m/d}(x)−V_{m/e}(F_{d/e}x) for e|d|m and x∈W_Div(d)(R)[q]. For m=1, Q_1(R) ≅ R, with q acting as 1.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring, possibly nonunital; m>0.

locator.where: Lemmas 2.9–2.10 and Remark 2.12, lines 483–549; printed wagner v5 pp. 11–12

api.name: QWitt.absolute_desc
api.statement: Maps to a q-FV system extend uniquely from the structural Witt maps.

api.name: QWitt.absolute_map
api.statement: Ring maps induce maps of initial systems; identity and composition hold.

api.name: QWitt.absolute_hom_ext
api.statement: System maps out of Q agree on the structural polynomial generators.

api.name: QWitt.F_comp_V_comp
api.statement: F and V compose, commute for coprime indices and satisfy the projection formula.

api.name: QWitt.teichmuller
api.statement: τ_m is the multiplicative composite R → W_Div(m)(R) → Q_m(R); F_{m/d}τ_m(r)=τ_d(r)^(m/d).

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_1
tests.statement: Q_1(R)=R and Q_m(0)=0, including nonunital inputs.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_3
tests.statement: At q=1, V_2F_2=2; this specialization need not be ordinary W_Div(2)(R).

targets.proofSketch: Verify that F and V preserve I_m using divisibility and coprime interchange in 1.4. The presentation gives the initial property and the remaining identities by descent from ordinary Witt operations.

targets.name: QWitt.absoluteGhost
targets.statement: For d|m define gh_{m/d}:Q_m(R) → R[q]/Φ_d(q) as F_{m/d} followed by the quotient by all proper-divisor V-images in Q_d. At d=m this is the first ghost; its target is R[q]/Φ_m(q). The Teichmüller image is r^(m/d) in the dth target.
hypotheses: R is commutative, possibly nonunital; m>0.

locator.where: §2.13, lines 552–580; printed wagner v5 pp. 12–13

api.name: QWitt.ghost_quotient
api.statement: ker gh_1 is the ideal generated by V_p-images for prime p|m.

api.name: QWitt.ghost_F
api.statement: gh_{m/d}=gh_1 F_{m/d}.

api.name: QWitt.ghost_V
api.statement: gh_{m/d} V_n is zero unless n divides m/d; when it does it is n times the appropriate source ghost.

api.name: QWitt.ghost_map
api.statement: Ghosts commute with coefficient maps.

tests.name: QWitt.absoluteGhost_1
tests.statement: For m=2 over ℤ, gh_1 evaluates q at −1 and kills V_2(1)=1+q.

tests.name: QWitt.absoluteGhost_2
tests.statement: At m=1 there are no proper V-images and Φ_1=q−1; the ghost is id_R.

tests.name: QWitt.absoluteGhost_3
tests.statement: Reduction q↦1 from Q_2 to Q_1 does not extend the ordinary restriction W_2→W_1: it sends V_2(1) to 2 whereas ordinary restriction sends it to 0.

targets.proofSketch: First quotient the defining ideal and all prime V-images; the cyclotomic ideal contract identifies the result, treating m=1 directly. Compose with F for the other ghosts.

targets.name: QWitt.absolute_verschiebungResolution
targets.statement: If p_1,…,p_r are the distinct prime factors of m, put p_J=∏_{j∈J}p_j. The augmented complex with ⊕_{|J|=k}Q_{m/p_J}(R) in chain degree k, Q_m(R) in degree 0 and quotient R[q]/Φ_m(q) is exact. Deletion of j∈J has coefficient (−1)^{#{i∈J:i<j}}V_{p_j}. In particular every V_n:Q_{m/n}(R) → Q_m(R) is injective.
hypotheses: R may be nonunital; m>0; an ordering of distinct prime divisors is fixed only to write signs.

locator.where: Proposition 2.15, Remark 2.16, Lemmas 2.17–2.18 and Corollary 2.19, lines 591–1004; printed wagner v5 pp. 13–19

api.name: QWitt.verschiebungResolution_perm
api.statement: Reordering primes gives the signed permutation chain isomorphism.

api.name: QWitt.verschiebung_injective
api.statement: All absolute Verschiebungen are injective without a torsion assumption.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_verschiebungResolution_1
tests.statement: For m=6, the first maps are Q_1 → Q_3⊕Q_2 → Q_6, x↦(−V_3x,V_2x), then (a,b)↦V_2a+V_3b; the composite is zero.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_verschiebungResolution_2
tests.statement: For m=1 the augmentation Q_1(R)→R is an isomorphism.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_verschiebungResolution_3
tests.statement: For m=2^a with a≥1, the resolution is 0→Q_{2^(a−1)}→Q_{2^a}→R[ζ_{2^a}]→0; a=0 is the separate m=1 augmentation, not a level with index 2^(−1).

targets.proofSketch: Prove the prime-power short exact sequence from the explicit ideal. For the general complex, use iterated mapping cones of its finite cube; split the prime-to-p V-directions after p-localization and compare the remaining direction with the prime-power case. Rational and prime-completed detection prove exactness; apply the same cube argument to kernels of V. The terminal object removed from the reverse-inclusion cube is ∅.

targets.name: QWitt.absolute_localization_torsion
targets.statement: Q_m commutes with integer localization and with localization R[U⁻¹] at τ_m(U). If R is p-torsion-free, so is Q_m(R); if R has bounded p-primary torsion, so does Q_m(R). If R is p-torsion-free for every p|m, its q-Witt ghosts are jointly injective.
hypotheses: R is commutative, possibly nonunital; multiplicative localization at elements uses the corresponding unital algebra or unitization; p is any prime.

locator.where: Corollaries 2.20, 2.22 and Lemmas 2.21, 2.23, lines 1006–1080; printed wagner v5 pp. 19–21

api.name: QWitt.absolute_localize
api.statement: Q_m(R)[τ_m(U)⁻¹] ≅ Q_m(R[U⁻¹]).

api.name: QWitt.absolute_boundedTorsion
api.statement: A finite bound on p-primary torsion of R gives a bound for each fixed m; no uniform bound in m is asserted.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_localization_torsion_1
tests.statement: For R=ℤ and m=2, the ghosts ℤ[q]/(q²−1)→ℤ×ℤ are jointly injective.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_localization_torsion_2
tests.statement: For R=𝔽₂,m=2, V_2(1) is nonzero by 3.4 but both ghosts vanish on it; dropping the torsion hypothesis fails.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_localization_torsion_3
tests.statement: For m=1 the sole ghost is id_R even when R has torsion.

targets.proofSketch: Induct along 3.4; localize first to ℤ_(p), where prime-to-p V maps split by ℓ⁻¹F_ℓ. Kernels killed by the other F maps and first ghost lie in im V_p. Apply this to torsion elements, bounding the exponents inductively.

targets.name: QWitt.absolute_completion
targets.statement: If the derived p-completion R̂_p is discrete, Q_m(R)^∧_p ≅ Q_m(R̂_p). If this holds for each p|m, then Q_m(R)^∧_{(q^n−1)} is discrete for every n>0. If R has bounded p-primary torsion for every p|m, Q_m(R) has bounded (q^n−1)-power torsion.
hypotheses: R is commutative, possibly nonunital; m,n>0; p is prime.

locator.where: Corollaries 2.24, 2.26 and Lemma 2.27, lines 1083–1190; printed wagner v5 pp. 21–23

api.name: QWitt.absolute_completion_natural
api.statement: Comparisons commute with F, V, ghosts and maps of R.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_completion_1
tests.statement: For R=ℤ,m=2, p-completion gives ℤ_p[q]/(q²−1).

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_completion_2
tests.statement: For m=1, (q^n−1) acts as zero and its derived completion is R.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_completion_3
tests.statement: Discreteness of R̂_p alone is not declared a bounded-torsion hypothesis; the two conclusions have distinct assumptions.

targets.proofSketch: Complete the finite resolution 3.4 and induct. On R[ζ_d], compare radicals of (q^n−1) with (p) when d/gcd(d,n) is a nontrivial p-power, use the unit ideal for at least two prime factors, and the zero ideal for d|n. The same argument with annihilator bounds gives bounded torsion.

targets.name: QWitt.absolute_witt_injective
targets.statement: The natural map W_Div(m)(R) → Q_m(R) is injective for every commutative ring R, including nonunital R. For an exact sequence 0→J→R→R′→0 of such rings, 0→Q_m(J)→Q_m(R)→Q_m(R′)→0 is exact as additive groups.
hypotheses: m>0; J is the kernel ring, with no unit required.

locator.where: Proposition 2.28, Corollary 2.29 and Lemma 2.30, lines 1194–1303; printed wagner v5 pp. 23–26

api.name: QWitt.absolute_pLocalDecomposition
api.statement: For R a ℤ_(p)-algebra and m=p^a n with gcd(n,p)=1, Q_m(R) ≅ ∏_{d|n} Q_{p^a}(R)⊗_{ℤ_(p)[q],q↦q^d}ℤ_(p)[q]/Φ_d(q^(p^a)).

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_witt_injective_1
tests.statement: For R=0 the injection and exact sequence are zero maps between zero objects.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_witt_injective_2
tests.statement: For m=2,R=𝔽₂, the element V_2(1) stays nonzero, despite its zero ghosts.

tests.name: QWitt.absolute_witt_injective_3
tests.statement: For m=1 the assertion is the original short exact sequence.

targets.proofSketch: The resolution proves exactness on kernel rings. Prove the displayed p-local decomposition by truncated universal properties and 1.6; reduce injectivity to prime powers, where the explicit ideal in 3.2 and coefficient comparison give injectivity. Localize at every prime to conclude.

layers.examples: Q_1(R)=R with q=1; Q_2(ℤ)=ℤ[q]/(q²−1); nonunital zero and square-zero rings remain included.

layers.title: Relative q-Witt rings and Λ comparison

targets.name: QWitt.lambdaComparison
targets.statement: For any arithmetic Λ-ring A let s_m:A[q]/(q^m−1)→Q_m(A) be the polynomial extension of the coaction A→W_Div(m)(A). Construct c_m:Q_m(A)→A[q]/(q^m−1) with c_m s_m=ψ_m, c_d F_{m/d}=reduction c_m and c_m V_{m/d}=[m/d]_{q^d}c_d. If all ψ_n are injective, c_m identifies Q_m(A) with ∑_{d|m}[d]_{q^(m/d)}ψ_{m/d}(A)[q]/(q^m−1). For perfect A, s_m and c_m are isomorphisms.
hypotheses: A is a commutative unital arithmetic Λ-ring; m>0.

locator.where: Lemmas 2.33–2.34, Corollary 2.35, Proposition 2.36 and Corollary 2.37, lines 1348–1468; printed wagner v5 pp. 27–29

api.name: QWitt.lambdaCoordinates
api.statement: Every x∈W_Div(m)(A) has a unique expansion ∑_{d|m}V_d s_{m/d}(a_d); define ε_d by its final coefficient.

api.name: QWitt.lambdaComparison_natural
api.statement: Both comparison maps commute with Λ-maps.

tests.name: QWitt.lambdaComparison_1
tests.statement: For A=ℤ,m=2, c_2 and s_2 are inverse isomorphisms and V_2(1) maps to 1+q.

tests.name: QWitt.lambdaComparison_2
tests.statement: For toric ℤ[T], c_2 has image ℤ[T²,q]+(1+q)ℤ[T,q] inside ℤ[T,q]/(q²−1); it is not the whole ring.

tests.name: QWitt.lambdaComparison_3
tests.statement: For m=1 both comparisons are identities.

targets.proofSketch: Use triangular Witt coordinates to define ε, first on free torsion-free Λ-rings and then by their reflexive presentations. The displayed formula is multiplicative after cyclotomic projection on a torsion-free universal ring. Descend to Q using 3.2; ghost injectivity and 2.4 give the image assertion.

targets.name: QWitt.RelativeFVSystem
targets.statement: For a Λ-ring A and unital A-algebra R, a relative q-FV system has A[q]-algebras E_m receiving Q_m(R)⊗_{Q_m(A),c_m}A[q]/(q^m−1), with compatible A[q]-algebra F and A[q]-linear V satisfying FV=m/d and VF=[m/d]_{q^d}. Define its morphisms by commutation with these maps.
hypotheses: A is any arithmetic Λ-ring; R is any commutative unital A-algebra; d|m.

locator.where: Definition 2.40, lines 1504–1512; printed wagner v5 p. 30

api.name: RelativeFVSystem.mk
api.statement: Structural maps and compatible F,V satisfying the two relations construct a system.

api.name: RelativeFVSystem.hom_ext
api.statement: Morphisms are determined by their component maps.

api.name: RelativeFVSystem.truncate
api.statement: Restriction to any divisor-closed set preserves the notion.

tests.name: QWitt.RelativeFVSystem_1
tests.statement: For R=A, E_m=A[q]/(q^m−1), reduction F and multiplication V satisfy the definition. At m=2,d=1, F_2V_2(1)=2 and V_2F_2(1)=1+q; replacing the latter q-integer by 2 fails.

tests.name: QWitt.RelativeFVSystem_2
tests.statement: For R=0 all components may be zero rings, over any A.

tests.name: QWitt.RelativeFVSystem_3
tests.statement: For toric A=R=ℤ[T], m=2,d=1, F_2 sends the right-hand scalar T to T in E_1=ℤ[T], whereas a ψ_2-semilinear substitute sends it to T². Thus the relative F is A[q]-linear.

targets.proofSketch: Use c_m to specify the scalar action; requiring compatibility with every V is additional data beyond the tensor product at a single level.

targets.name: QWitt.relative
targets.statement: The category in 4.2 has initial object Q_m(R/A). It is the tensor product there modulo the ideal generated by V_{m/d}(xy)⊗1−V_{m/d}(x)⊗c_d(y), for x∈Q_d(R), y∈Q_d(A). Lifts of c_d(y) modulo q^m−1 give the same generator because V_{m/d}(x) is killed by q^d−1. It has functorial F,V, multiplicative τ_m and composition, coprime interchange and projection laws.
hypotheses: A is any arithmetic Λ-ring; R any commutative unital A-algebra; m>0.

locator.where: Lemmas 2.41–2.42 and Remark 2.43, lines 1513–1559; printed wagner v5 pp. 30–31

api.name: QWitt.relative_desc
api.statement: There is a unique compatible map to any relative q-FV system.

api.name: QWitt.relative_map
api.statement: A-algebra maps give maps of systems, preserving identity and composition.

api.name: QWitt.relative_hom_ext
api.statement: Maps of systems agree when their structural maps agree.

api.name: QWitt.relative_teichmuller_F
api.statement: F_{m/d}τ_m(r)=τ_d(r)^(m/d).

api.name: QWitt.relative_truncation
api.statement: The same initial property holds on every divisor-closed set; Div(m) depends only on Λ_{p|m}.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_1
tests.statement: Q_1(R/A)=R and Q_m(0/A)=0.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_2
tests.statement: Q_m(A/A)=A[q]/(q^m−1), even for a nonperfect A.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_3
tests.statement: Take toric A=ℤ[T], R=A[X], m=2 and d=1. In B=Q_2(R)⊗_{Q_2(A),c_2}A[q]/(q²−1), the two expressions V_2(TX)⊗1 and V_2(X)⊗T differ. A map B→𝔽₂[ε]/(ε²) sends them to ε and 0: on Q_2(R) use the polynomial image in 4.1 and send b to b(0,0,1) mod 2 plus ε times half the TX-coefficient of b(T,X,1), modulo 2; on A[q] send T to 0 and q to 1. Coefficients of monomials with an odd exponent are even; the cross terms in the TX-coefficient of a product are divisible by 4, so this is a ring map and agrees with c_2 on Q_2(A). The defining ideal contains exactly their difference, from x=X,y=T, so it enforces V-linearity.

targets.proofSketch: Check that all F and V preserve the ideal, using the comparison compatibilities in 4.1 and separate cases p|m/d and p∤m/d. The universal property gives maps and laws without requiring flatness of A.

targets.name: QWitt.relativeGhost
targets.statement: For d|m construct gh_{m/d}:Q_m(R/A)→R^(d)⊗_A A[q]/Φ_d(q). It factors as F_{m/d} then the first ghost of Q_d. The first ghost gh_1 at level m is the quotient by the ideal generated by all proper-divisor V-images.
hypotheses: A is any Λ-ring; R is an A-algebra; d|m and d,m>0.

locator.where: §2.44, lines 1565–1572; printed wagner v5 p. 31

api.name: QWitt.relativeGhost_tmul
api.statement: On structural x⊗a, gh_{m/d} sends x to its ordinary (m/d)th Witt ghost in the R factor, and a to the A[q]/Φ_d factor.

api.name: QWitt.relativeGhost_natural
api.statement: Ghosts commute with maps of A-algebras and Λ-base change.

tests.name: QWitt.relativeGhost_1
tests.statement: At d=m, gh_1(s_m(a))=a⊗1=1⊗ψ_m(a). For toric A=R=ℤ[T] and m=2, the identification r⊗b↦ψ_2(r)b sends both sides to T², also after adjoining ζ_2. The reversed formula would assert T⁴=T, which is false.

tests.name: QWitt.relativeGhost_2
tests.statement: At m=d=1, R^(1)[ζ_1]=R and the map is identity.

tests.name: QWitt.relativeGhost_3
tests.statement: Over A=ℤ the twisted targets identify with the absolute ghost targets.

targets.proofSketch: Tensor the absolute ghosts with the scalar cyclotomic quotient and verify that every relative generator in 4.3 vanishes. The tensor balancing equation forces ψ_d, with no choice of inverse Adams operation.

targets.name: QWitt.relative_baseChange
targets.statement: For any Λ-map A→A′ and A-algebra R there is a canonical A′[q]-algebra isomorphism Q_m(R/A)⊗_A A′ ≅ Q_m(R⊗_A A′/A′), compatible with F,V,τ and twisted ghosts. No flatness is required.
hypotheses: A,A′ are arithmetic Λ-rings; R is any A-algebra; m>0.

locator.where: Lemma 2.46, lines 1583–1620; printed wagner v5 pp. 31–32

api.name: QWitt.polynomial_image
api.statement: For toric A[T_i], Q_m(A[T_i]/A) identifies with ∑_{d|m}[d]_{q^(m/d)}A[T_i^(m/d),q]/(q^m−1).

api.name: QWitt.reflexive_coequalizer
api.statement: Q_m(−/A) preserves reflexive coequalizers and filtered colimits.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_baseChange_1
tests.statement: A′=A gives the identity comparison, and A′=0 gives zero.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_baseChange_2
tests.statement: For R=A[T], m=2 the polynomial-image formula commutes with any Λ-base map.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_baseChange_3
tests.statement: Base change here uses a Λ-map of bases; an arbitrary ring map does not specify the required ψ-compatible scalar action.

targets.proofSketch: First identify the polynomial image using the maps in 4.1 and the relative relations. Prove base change there directly; then use the initial property to preserve reflexive coequalizers of polynomial presentations. A bare appeal to the tensor universal property would omit the Witt structure on the new coefficients.

targets.name: QWitt.perfectCover_comparison
targets.statement: If A is perfectly covered, all relative V are injective, the relative version of the exact resolution 3.4 has quotient R^(m)[ζ_m], and for a relatively perfect Λ-A-algebra R the maps s_{m/A}:R^(m)[q]/(q^m−1)→Q_m(R/A) and c_{m/A}:Q_m(R/A)→R[q]/(q^m−1) are isomorphisms with composite ψ_{m/A}. For any Λ-A-algebra R both maps exist with that composite without the perfection hypotheses.
hypotheses: A is a Λ-ring; existence of comparisons assumes R is a Λ-A-algebra; injectivity and exactness assume A perfectly covered; isomorphisms also assume R relatively perfect.

locator.where: §2.45 and Remark 2.47, lines 1573–1643; printed wagner v5 pp. 31–32

api.name: QWitt.perfectBase_absolute
api.statement: If A is perfect, the natural Q_m(R)→Q_m(R/A) is an isomorphism for every R/A.

api.name: QWitt.relativeComparison_natural
api.statement: The comparisons commute with Λ-A-algebra maps and Λ-base change.

tests.name: QWitt.perfectCover_comparison_1
tests.statement: For R=A, s_{m/A} is the standard identification even when A is only perfectly covered.

tests.name: QWitt.perfectCover_comparison_2
tests.statement: For toric ℤ[T]/ℤ, relative perfection fails and c_2 misses T.

tests.name: QWitt.perfectCover_comparison_3
tests.statement: For A=ℤ all relative V are injective even on torsion R.

targets.proofSketch: Use 4.5 and A→A^perf, reduce to the absolute perfect-base case via 4.1, then descend exactness and isomorphisms by faithful flatness. Keep existence separate from the statements requiring descent.

layers.examples: Relative constructions exist before perfect coverage is assumed. Twisted ghosts retain the Adams operation of the base.

layers.title: Étale base change, finiteness and relative completions

targets.name: QWitt.etale
targets.statement: For every étale A-algebra map R→R′, Q_m(R/A)→Q_m(R′/A) is étale. For d|m its F-square is a pushout: Q_m(R′/A)⊗_{Q_m(R/A),F_{m/d}}Q_d(R/A) ≅ Q_d(R′/A). The ordinary tensor is also the derived tensor since the changed factor is étale and flat.
hypotheses: A is any arithmetic Λ-ring; R,R′ any A-algebras; m>0.

locator.where: Proposition 2.48 and Lemma 2.50, lines 1651–1712; printed wagner v5 pp. 33–34

api.name: QWitt.etale_wittBaseChange
api.statement: W_Div(m)(R′)⊗_{W_Div(m)(R)}Q_m(R/A) ≅ Q_m(R′/A).

api.name: QWitt.etale_natural
api.statement: The pushout comparison is natural and compatible with chains of divisors.

tests.name: QWitt.etale_1
tests.statement: For R′=R the comparison is identity.

tests.name: QWitt.etale_2
tests.statement: At m=1 it is the original étale algebra R′ over R.

tests.name: QWitt.etale_3
tests.statement: No perfect-cover, Noetherian or F-finiteness hypothesis is added to this theorem.

targets.proofSketch: Apply ordinary Witt étale base change to the generators and relations in 3.2 and 4.3, giving the displayed Witt-base-change comparison. Étaleness and the F-pushout then follow from 1.6.

targets.name: QWitt.ghost_etalePushout
targets.statement: For d|m and an étale A-algebra map R→R′, the square from Q_m(R/A)→Q_m(R′/A) to R^(d)[ζ_d]→R′^(d)[ζ_d], with vertical maps gh_{m/d}, is a pushout of rings and of derived commutative algebras.
hypotheses: A any arithmetic Λ-ring; R→R′ étale over A; d|m.

locator.where: Corollary 2.51, lines 1715–1730; printed wagner v5 p. 34

api.name: QWitt.ghost_etalePushout_map
api.statement: The comparison on pure tensors is induced by the coefficient map and the relative ghost.

tests.name: QWitt.ghost_etalePushout_1
tests.statement: At m=d=1 the square is the identity vertical square.

tests.name: QWitt.ghost_etalePushout_2
tests.statement: For R=A it identifies Q_m(R′/A)⊗_{A[q]/(q^m−1)}A[ζ_d] with R′^(d)[ζ_d].

tests.name: QWitt.ghost_etalePushout_3
tests.statement: With R′=R/(x), flatness may fail; this is not a derived pushout assertion for arbitrary maps.

targets.proofSketch: Reduce to d=m by 5.1 and present the first ghost as the cokernel of all proper V-images. Flatness of the étale Q-map makes the ordinary quotient pushout the derived one.

targets.name: QWitt.relative_torsion_completion
targets.statement: For a perfectly covered A and any R/A, all conclusions of 3.5 and 3.6 about integer torsion, joint ghost injectivity and discrete completions hold relatively, with ghosts in R^(d)[ζ_d]. In particular Q_m(R/A)^∧_p ≅ Q_m(R̂_p/A) when R̂_p is discrete, and Q_m(R/A)^∧_{(q^n−1)} is discrete if R̂_p is discrete for all p|m. Bounded p-primary torsion of R for all p|m gives bounded (q^n−1)-power torsion.
hypotheses: A perfectly covered; m,n>0; p prime. Ghost injectivity assumes R p-torsion-free for all p|m; integer torsion statements keep the same prime-specific hypotheses as 3.5.

locator.where: Remark 2.47, lines 1621–1643, with Corollaries 2.22, 2.24, 2.26; §4.19 proof, lines 3123–3127; printed wagner v5 pp. 20–22, 32, 63

api.name: QWitt.relative_completeBaseChange
api.statement: Completed scalar extension to A^perf computes the corresponding completion after perfect-base comparison; complete faithful-flat descent detects discreteness.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_torsion_completion_1
tests.statement: For R=A,m=1, all comparisons reduce to those for A.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_torsion_completion_2
tests.statement: For A=ℤ the statement agrees with 3.6.

tests.name: QWitt.relative_torsion_completion_3
tests.statement: No relative V-injectivity or torsion/completion descent is asserted for an arbitrary Λ-base.

targets.proofSketch: Use the faithful-flat perfect cover and 4.5 for torsion and exactness. For completions, use completed derived scalar extension, not uncompleted tensor interchange with infinite limits; apply complete faithful-flat descent and bounded-torsion comparison from the supplier contracts.

targets.name: QWitt.finiteType
targets.statement: If R is a finite type ℤ-algebra, Q_m(R) is a finite type ℤ[q]/(q^m−1)-algebra and hence Noetherian. For the toric polynomial ring R₀=ℤ[T_1,…,T_r], R₀[q]/(q^m−1) is finite over the image of c_m. Relative q-Witt functors commute with filtered colimits and reflexive polynomial presentations.
hypotheses: m>0; finite type and finitely many variables are required only for the finiteness statements.

locator.where: Corollary 2.39 and proof, lines 1485–1495; Lemma 2.46 proof, lines 1588–1620; printed wagner v5 pp. 29, 31–32

api.name: QWitt.polynomial_finite
api.statement: The image contains ℤ[T_1^m,…,T_r^m,q]/(q^m−1), over which R₀[q]/(q^m−1) is finite.

tests.name: QWitt.finiteType_1
tests.statement: With r=0 this is the finite free rank-m algebra ℤ[q]/(q^m−1).

tests.name: QWitt.finiteType_2
tests.statement: At m=2,r=1, 1,T generate ℤ[T,q]/(q²−1) over the subring containing T².

tests.name: QWitt.finiteType_3
tests.statement: Infinitely many variables are allowed for base change, but are not declared Noetherian.

targets.proofSketch: Use the image formula 4.1 and integral monomials for the polynomial case, then descend through a finite presentation. Filtered colimits and reflexive coequalizers follow from the algebraic universal properties.

layers.examples: Identity maps, prime-power indices and a characteristic-two ghost kernel test the limits of étale and torsion claims.

layers.title: Completed coefficient Frobenius and cyclotomic overlaps

targets.name: QWitt.completedEtaleFrobenius
targets.statement: For every prime p, a perfectly covered Λ-ring A and étale R/A, the ordinary p-completion R̂_p has a unique continuous ring endomorphism φ_p extending ψ_p:A→A→R̂_p and reducing to x↦x^p on R/p. Its linearization (R̂_p⊗^L_{A,ψ_p}A)^∧_p→R̂_p, r⊗a↦φ_p(r)a, is an equivalence. All rings and completed tensor products in this statement are discrete and agree with ordinary completed tensor products.
hypotheses: A perfectly covered; R étale over A; p prime. No Λ-structure or Frobenius lift on uncompleted R is assumed.

locator.where: §2.7, lines 647–658; printed wagner-habiro v2 pp. 15–16

api.name: completedEtaleFrobenius_mod
api.statement: φ_p(r) mod p = r^p for r∈R; the map is ψ_p-semilinear over A.

api.name: completedEtaleFrobenius_natural
api.statement: Étale A-algebra maps commute with φ_p on p-completions.

api.name: completedEtaleFrobenius_iterate
api.statement: Iterated linearizations for ψ_{p^a} are equivalences, compatible with composition.

api.name: completedEtaleFrobenius_ordinary
api.statement: The derived completed tensor equals completion of the ordinary twisted tensor.

tests.name: QWitt.completedEtaleFrobenius_1
tests.statement: For R=A, the linearization is the canonical equivalence of the ψ_p-twisted base with A after completion. If p is invertible in A, both completions are zero; no prime is discarded.

tests.name: QWitt.completedEtaleFrobenius_2
tests.statement: For A=ℤ,R=ℤ×ℤ,p=2, φ_2 is identity on ℤ₂×ℤ₂ and reduces to the square map.

tests.name: QWitt.completedEtaleFrobenius_3
tests.statement: For R=ℤ[T] over A=ℤ, the coordinate lift T↦T² exists but its linearization is not an equivalence modulo 2: T is outside its image. Étaleness cannot be replaced by smoothness.

targets.proofSketch: Lift the relative Frobenius modulo p uniquely through the nilpotent p-power thickenings using formal étaleness. The inverse limit gives φ_p. Perfect coverage makes A and R torsion-free and ψ_p flat; completed tensor products are discrete by complete flatness. Modulo p the linearization is étale relative Frobenius, an isomorphism; derived Nakayama gives the equivalence.

targets.name: QWitt.cyclotomicCompletedFrobenius
targets.statement: For A,R,p as in 6.1 and every d>0 there is a natural A[q]-linear equivalence ((R̂_p⊗^L_{A,ψ_{pd}}A)[q])^∧_{(p,Φ_{pd})} ≃ ((R̂_p⊗^L_{A,ψ_d}A)[q])^∧_{(p,Φ_d)}, induced by r⊗a↦φ_p(r)⊗a and q↦q. It agrees with ordinary completed tensor products. Iteration composes these maps for d,pd,…,p^a d.
hypotheses: A perfectly covered; R étale over A; p prime; d>0.

locator.where: §2.7 and Theorem 2.9 proof, lines 647–661 and 709–716; printed wagner-habiro v2 pp. 15–17

api.name: cyclotomicCompletedFrobenius_q
api.statement: The equivalence fixes q and the right A-factor.

api.name: cyclotomicCompletedFrobenius_ideals
api.statement: The ideals (p,Φ_d) and (p,Φ_{pd}) have equal radicals in A[q], giving the same derived completion functor.

api.name: cyclotomicCompletedFrobenius_baseChange
api.statement: The equivalence is the ψ_d-base change of 6.1 followed by the common completion; it commutes with morphisms of étale A-algebras.

tests.name: QWitt.cyclotomicCompletedFrobenius_1
tests.statement: For p=2,d=1, Φ_1=q−1 and Φ_2=q+1 become equal modulo 2.

tests.name: QWitt.cyclotomicCompletedFrobenius_2
tests.statement: For p=3,d=1, Φ_3 mod 3=(q−1)²; (3,Φ_3) and (3,q−1) have the same radical but are not equal in ℤ[q].

tests.name: QWitt.cyclotomicCompletedFrobenius_3
tests.statement: For R=0 both sides are zero, and for R=A the map is the canonical twisted-base equivalence.

targets.proofSketch: Apply ψ_d scalar extension to 6.1: tensor balancing uses ψ_dψ_p=ψ_{pd}. Extend by q fixed. Equal radicals permit use of one completion topology; flatness of ψ_d and completed base change give the equivalence, without imposing p∤d.

targets.name: QWitt.completedGhostFrobenius
targets.statement: For pd|m, the reductions modulo p of gh_{m/(pd)} and gh_{m/d} commute with the bottom map R/p⊗_{A/p,ψ_{pd}}(A/p)[q]/Φ_{pd}→R/p⊗_{A/p,ψ_d}(A/p)[q]/Φ_d, r⊗a↦r^p⊗a, q↦q. The deformation of this bottom map on the common (p,Φ_d)-completion is exactly 6.2.
hypotheses: A perfectly covered; R étale over A; p prime; pd|m.

locator.where: Theorem 2.9 proof, lines 679–721; printed wagner-habiro v2 pp. 16–17

api.name: completedGhostFrobenius_teichmuller
api.statement: The two paths on τ_m(r) give r^(m/d)⊗1.

api.name: completedGhostFrobenius_deformation
api.statement: The comparison is characterized by the indicated reduction and unique étale lifting, compatibly with iterations.

tests.name: QWitt.completedGhostFrobenius_1
tests.statement: For m=p,d=1, the upper Teichmüller value r maps to r^p, matching the bottom ghost.

tests.name: QWitt.completedGhostFrobenius_2
tests.statement: For A=R=ℤ and p=2 this is the q-fixed overlap between q=−1 and q=1 modulo 2.

tests.name: QWitt.completedGhostFrobenius_3
tests.statement: For A=R=ℤ,p=2,d=1,m=2, the deformed bottom map sends q=1+h to 1+h in ℤ₂[[h]]. Substitution q↦q² instead gives 1+2h+h², a different value; the deformation must fix q.

targets.proofSketch: The ordinary Witt ghosts in characteristic p satisfy w_{pn}=w_n^p. Descend this identity through the relative presentation and the cyclotomic quotient. Use 5.2 for the étale ghost algebras and unique formal lifting to identify the completed map.

layers.examples: The coefficient map fixes q. For p=3,d=1 its two completion ideals have equal radicals but need not be equal.

layers.title: Positive-degree q-Witt systems

targets.name: QWitt.DifferentialVSystem
targets.statement: For A a Λ-ring and R/A define a q-V system of nonnegative differential graded A[q]-algebras P_m: each has xy=(−1)^(ij)yx for homogeneous x∈P_m^i,y∈P_m^j, and x²=0 whenever i is odd, receives Q_m(R/A)→P_m⁰, and has graded A[q]-linear V_{m/d} extending degree-zero V, with identity and composition laws, V(ω dη)=V(ω)dV(η), and V(ω)dτ_m(r)=V(ωτ_d(r)^(m/d−1))dV(τ_d(r)). Morphisms preserve all data.
hypotheses: A any arithmetic Λ-ring; R any A-algebra; homogeneous ω,η in the indicated source; r∈R; d|m.

locator.where: Definition 3.1, lines 1822–1838; printed wagner v5 p. 37

api.name: DifferentialVSystem.mk
api.statement: The specified degree-zero map, V and identities construct an object.

api.name: DifferentialVSystem.hom_ext
api.statement: Component DGA maps determine system maps.

api.name: DifferentialVSystem.V_d
api.statement: V_n d = n d V_n.

api.name: DifferentialVSystem.truncate
api.statement: Restrict to arbitrary divisor-closed positive indices.

tests.name: QWitt.DifferentialVSystem_1
tests.statement: At level 1, the exterior de Rham algebra Ω*_{A[T]/A}, with q=1 and V_1=id, satisfies the multiplication conditions: dT∧dT=0 and d(T²)=2T dT. A symmetric algebra on dT with nonzero square would fail.

tests.name: QWitt.DifferentialVSystem_2
tests.statement: Over 𝔽₂ a graded commutative algebra with a degree-one element u satisfying u²≠0 is excluded by strict alternation.

tests.name: QWitt.DifferentialVSystem_3
tests.statement: For A=R=ℤ and m=1, take P=ℤ[u] with |u|=2 and zero differential. The quotient by (u²) retains u≠0 and has u²=0; it satisfies both multiplication conditions. In Ω*_{ℤ[T]/ℤ}, the graded ideal (T) is not differential because dT is outside it, so quotienting only by (T) cannot induce a differential.

targets.proofSketch: Use the associative DG carriers, imposing the displayed graded commutativity and strict odd alternation as conditions on their multiplication. The projection identity with ω=1 and the relation (q^d−1)P_d=0 prove V_n d=n dV_n; no integer is inverted.

targets.name: QWitt.differential
targets.statement: For every A,R as in 7.1 construct the initial q-V system Q_mΩ*_{R/A}. Degree zero is canonically Q_m(R/A), and Q_1Ω*_{R/A}≅Ω*_{R/A}. The natural de Rham DGA map Ω*_{Q_m(R/A)/A[q]}→Q_mΩ* is surjective. At level m the defining differential ideal is generated by all lifted relations ∑V(w_j)dV(x_{j1})⋯dV(x_{jk}) whenever ∑w_j dx_{j1}⋯dx_{jk}=0 at a proper divisor, and the V-Teichmüller relations of 7.1.
hypotheses: A any Λ-ring; R any A-algebra; m>0; strict odd alternation including at 2.

locator.where: Proposition 3.12, Definition 3.13 and Remark 3.14, lines 1956–2010; printed wagner v5 pp. 40–41

api.name: QWitt.differential_desc
api.statement: Every q-V system receives a unique system map from QΩ.

api.name: QWitt.differential_hom_ext
api.statement: Maps agree on elements x₀dx₁⋯dx_k and the structural data.

api.name: QWitt.differential_map
api.statement: A-algebra maps induce DGA maps; filtered colimits and reflexive polynomial presentations are preserved.

api.name: QWitt.differential_V_monomial
api.statement: V(w dx₁⋯dx_k)=V(w)dV(x₁)⋯dV(x_k).

tests.name: QWitt.differential_2
tests.statement: For R=A the complex is A[q]/(q^m−1) in degree zero.

tests.name: QWitt.differential_3
tests.statement: For m=1,R=A[T], d(T²)=2T dT and dT∧dT=0, also at residue characteristic 2.

targets.proofSketch: Induct on m through its proper divisors and quotient the supplied de Rham algebra by the stated differential ideal. All generators have positive degree, preserving degree zero. Lifting polynomial differential expressions proves existence of V and initiality.

targets.name: QWitt.DifferentialFVSystem
targets.statement: A differential q-FV system is a q-V system with graded A[q]-algebra F_{m/d} extending F in degree zero, F_1=id, composition, coprime F/V interchange, FV=m/d, VF=[m/d]_{q^d}, F d V=d, V(ωFη)=V(ω)η and F(dτ_m(r))=τ_d(r)^(m/d−1)dτ_d(r).
hypotheses: A any Λ-ring; R any A-algebra; d|m. F is not required to commute with d.

locator.where: Definition 3.6 and Lemma 3.7 proof, lines 1893–1929; printed wagner v5 p. 39

api.name: DifferentialFVSystem.mk
api.statement: A q-V system and the displayed graded maps and relations construct an object.

api.name: DifferentialFVSystem.hom_ext
api.statement: A morphism is determined by its component graded algebra maps.

api.name: DifferentialFVSystem.d_F
api.statement: d F_n = n F_n d, derived from F d V=d and VF=[n]_{q^d}.

api.name: DifferentialFVSystem.forget
api.statement: Forget F to obtain a q-V system; no equivalence of these two categories is asserted.

tests.name: QWitt.DifferentialFVSystem_1
tests.statement: At m=2,R=ℤ[T], F_2(dτ_2(T))=T dT but d(F_2τ_2(T))=2T dT.

tests.name: QWitt.DifferentialFVSystem_2
tests.statement: For A=ℤ, R=ℤ[T], m=3 and d=1, F_3(dτ_3(T))=T²dT whereas d(F_3τ_3(T))=3T²dT. Reducing these values modulo 3 gives the nonzero form T²dT and zero, respectively; the scaled differential law cannot be replaced by the chain-map law.

tests.name: QWitt.DifferentialFVSystem_3
tests.statement: At m=d=1, F_1=id on Ω*_{ℤ[T]/ℤ}, so dF_1(T)=F_1d(T)=dT. This boundary has scale factor 1 and requires no prime Frobenius step.

targets.proofSketch: Store exactly the graded identities and prove the differential formula by FdV and VF; (q^d−1)=0 on the target converts the q-integer to n. The source proof, rather than its misprinted display, fixes the formula.

targets.name: QWitt.verschiebungPrimeDifferential
targets.statement: In every q-V system over R/A, for p|m and x∈Q_{m/p}(R/A), dV_p(x^p)=V_p(x^(p−1))dV_p(x). On absolute q-Witt vectors the map γ_p on im V_p defined by γ_p(V_p x)=p^(p−2)V_p(x^p) is well-defined and satisfies pγ_p(v)=v^p; the differential of every q-V system is a derivation compatible with this operation after passing from absolute to relative degree zero.
hypotheses: A any Λ-ring; R any A-algebra; p prime dividing m; a q-V system as in 7.1 is given. No Frobenius on positive degrees is used.

locator.where: §3.3 and Lemma 3.4, lines 1849–1874; langer-zink Lemma 1.5, langer-zink line 601; printed wagner v5 p. 38; langer-zink July 2003 pp. 19–20

api.name: QWitt.VPD_teichmuller
api.statement: The V-Teichmüller identity supplies the relation for scalar multiples of Teichmüller lifts.

api.name: QWitt.VPD_add
api.statement: The relation is preserved under addition, using the integral binomial identity.

api.name: QWitt.VPD_noFrobenius
api.statement: The proof uses V and d only, so it is available before 7.5.

tests.name: QWitt.verschiebungPrimeDifferential_1
tests.statement: At p=2, γ_2(V_2x)=V_2(x²) and 2γ_2(V_2x)=(V_2x)²; no inverse of 2 occurs.

tests.name: QWitt.verschiebungPrimeDifferential_2
tests.statement: For x=0 both sides of the differential identity are zero.

tests.name: QWitt.verschiebungPrimeDifferential_3
tests.statement: On the first-ghost quotient all V-images vanish, so the identity reduces to zero; on Teichmüller generators it is exactly the V-Teichmüller condition.

targets.proofSketch: Prove the formula first on Teichmüller generators, then on sums by the integral binomial expansion, and finally on V_ℓ-generators by induction on m, including ℓ=p. This is the V-only adaptation of the three-step argument in langer-zink line 605; it does not use an unconstructed F. Absolute V-injectivity makes γ_p a function on its image; the relative assertion is the displayed identity, not a claim of relative V-injectivity.

targets.name: QWitt.frobeniusDifferential
targets.statement: For each p|m define an F_p-semilinear derivation θ_p:Q_m(R)→Q_{m/p}Ω¹_{R/ℤ} by θ_pτ_m(r)=τ_{m/p}(r)^(p−1)dτ_{m/p}(r), θ_p V_p=d, and, for ℓ≠p prime dividing m, p θ_pV_ℓ=dF_pV_ℓ and ℓ θ_pV_ℓ=V_ℓθ_p. It extends uniquely to graded F_p on the relative Q_mΩ*. These F make QΩ initial among differential q-FV systems.
hypotheses: A any arithmetic Λ-ring; R any A-algebra; m>0; p prime dividing m.

locator.where: Proposition 3.17, §§3.20–3.30, lines 2053–2549; langer-zink Proposition 1.3, langer-zink line 453 (July 2003 preprint); printed wagner v5 pp. 42–50; langer-zink July 2003 pp. 14–16

api.name: QWitt.theta_add_mul
api.statement: θ_p(x+y)=θ_p(x)+θ_p(y), θ_p(xy)=F_p(x)θ_p(y)+F_p(y)θ_p(x).

api.name: QWitt.frobeniusDifferential_monomial
api.statement: F_p(x₀dx₁⋯dx_k)=F_p(x₀)θ_p(x₁)⋯θ_p(x_k).

api.name: QWitt.frobeniusDifferential_unique
api.statement: The Teichmüller and V formulas determine all F; this is uniqueness on the initial object, not on every q-V system.

tests.name: QWitt.frobeniusDifferential_1
tests.statement: For R=ℤ[T] at m=p=2, θ_2(τ_2(T))=T dT without division by 2, and θ_2(V_2(T))=dT rather than 2dT.

tests.name: QWitt.frobeniusDifferential_2
tests.statement: For R=ℤ[T] at m=p=2, F_2(τ_2(T))=T², hence θ_2(τ_2(T)²)=2T³dT. An ordinary derivation with the same value on τ_2(T) would instead give 2T²dT; the F_2-semilinear product rule is essential.

tests.name: QWitt.frobeniusDifferential_3
tests.statement: At m=1 there is no prime step and F_1=id.

targets.proofSketch: Use the exact V-resolution to define θ on the sum of V-images. The cyclotomic quotient gives unique Teichmüller remainder representatives. Prove additivity and the derivation law by finite-type reduction, detection after localization and completion, and the already constructed proper-divisor operations. Check that θ kills the relative scalar and differential ideals, then use the de Rham universal property. Verify the system laws on the generators; no torsion-free assumption on R is used.

targets.name: QWitt.differentialGhost
targets.statement: Construct DGA maps gh_{m/d}:Q_mΩ*_{R/A}→Ω*_{R/A}⊗_{A,ψ_d}A[ζ_d]. On a form x₀dx₁⋯dx_k use the corresponding degree-zero ghost and its de Rham differential. In degree i the ghost of V_n has coefficient n^(i+1) on the components whose index divides the smaller level and is zero elsewhere.
hypotheses: A any Λ-ring; R any A-algebra; d|m; i≥0.

locator.where: §3.15, lines 2011–2041; printed wagner v5 pp. 41–42

api.name: QWitt.differentialGhost_d
api.statement: Ghosts commute with differential and multiplication.

api.name: QWitt.differentialGhost_F
api.statement: For n=m/d and e|d, n^i gh_{d/e}(F_nω)=gh_{m/e}(ω) for a degree-i form ω.

api.name: QWitt.differentialGhost_natural
api.statement: Ghosts commute with A-algebra maps and Λ-base change.

tests.name: QWitt.differentialGhost_1
tests.statement: At m=2, the degree-one d=1 component of V_2(dT) is 4dT, not 2dT.

tests.name: QWitt.differentialGhost_2
tests.statement: At m=1 the differential ghost is identity on Ω*_{R/A}.

tests.name: QWitt.differentialGhost_3
tests.statement: For A=ℤ,R=ℤ[T],m=2,d=1, gh_2(V_2(T))=2T in degree zero, whereas gh_2(V_2(dT))=4dT in degree one. A degree-independent coefficient 2 fails.

targets.proofSketch: Give the product of twisted de Rham algebras the q-V system whose degree-i V acts as n^(i+1) on surviving components; apply initiality 7.2. Compatibility with F follows from 7.5 and its Teichmüller and V generators.

targets.name: QWitt.differential_baseChange
targets.statement: For a Λ-map A→A′, Q_mΩ*_{R/A}⊗_A A′ ≅ Q_mΩ*_{R⊗_A A′/A′}. If R→R′ is étale over A, Q_m(R′/A)⊗_{Q_m(R/A)}Q_mΩ*_{R/A} ≅ Q_mΩ*_{R′/A}, with the unique DGA differential extending that on Q_mΩ*. Both comparisons preserve F,V,τ and ghosts.
hypotheses: A,A′ any Λ-rings; R any A-algebra; m>0. Étaleness is required in the second assertion only.

locator.where: Lemma 3.16 and Proposition 3.31, Lemma 3.32, lines 2044–2050 and 2552–2595; printed wagner v5 pp. 42, 50–51

api.name: QWitt.differential_etaleDescent
api.statement: The degreewise functors on affine étale algebras satisfy faithfully flat étale descent.

api.name: QWitt.differential_etaleDifferential
api.statement: For a nonnegative DGA P and an étale map P⁰→S, the graded scalar extension S⊗_{P⁰}P admits exactly one extending differential.

tests.name: QWitt.differential_baseChange_1
tests.statement: A′=A and R′=R give identity isomorphisms.

tests.name: QWitt.differential_baseChange_2
tests.statement: At m=1 both results are ordinary de Rham base change.

tests.name: QWitt.differential_baseChange_3
tests.statement: For A=ℤ,m=1, the étale localization ℤ[T]→ℤ[T,T⁻¹] has d(T⁻¹)=−T⁻²dT≠0. Defining the extended differential by s⊗ω↦s⊗dω would instead give zero on T⁻¹.

targets.proofSketch: Λ-base change follows from initiality and 4.5. For étale scalar extension use Ω*_{S/A[q]}⊗_{Ω*_{P⁰/A[q]}}P to define the differential. Transfer F and V using 5.1 and verify the Teichmüller and FdV identities by uniqueness of étale derivations. Module descent gives the degreewise sheaf property.

layers.examples: Frobenius is a graded algebra map. Its differential relation has a factor n, visible on dτ_2(T) already over ℤ[T].

layers.title: Complete framed difference calculus

targets.name: QWitt.framedGamma
targets.statement: For an étale framing □:A[T₁,…,T_r]→R over any commutative A, on R[[h]] with q=1+h construct unique continuous A[[h]]-algebra automorphisms γ_i congruent to id modulo h and extending T_j↦q^(δ_ij)T_j. They commute and γ_i−id has image in hT_i R[[h]]. Multiplication by hT_i is injective, so the quotient below is uniquely defined.
hypotheses: r≥0; A any commutative unital ring, without a Λ-structure requirement; R étale over the displayed polynomial algebra.

locator.where: §4.7, lines 2830–2848; pridham Definition 1.22, pridham line 371; scholze §3, scholze line 319; printed wagner v5 p. 57; pridham v4 p. 9; scholze v1 p. 6

api.name: framedGamma_coordinate
api.statement: γ_i(T_j)=q^(δ_ij)T_j and γ_i(a)=a.

api.name: framedGamma_inverse
api.statement: The inverse extends T_i↦q⁻¹T_i; q=1+h is a unit in A[[h]].

api.name: framedGamma_natural
api.statement: Framing-compatible étale maps commute with γ_i.

api.name: framedGamma_unique
api.statement: Reduction id and the coordinate formula determine γ_i.

tests.name: QWitt.framedGamma_1
tests.statement: For A[T], γ(T²)=q²T²=(1+2h+h²)T².

tests.name: QWitt.framedGamma_2
tests.statement: With no variables, R/A is étale and there are no γ_i; constants are fixed.

tests.name: QWitt.framedGamma_3
tests.statement: The polynomial ring A[T,q] does not make q invertible; the same coordinate map there need not be an automorphism. Completion is essential.

targets.proofSketch: Lift the coordinate automorphism successively through R[h]/h^n by formal étaleness; lift the inverse too. Uniqueness proves commuting and naturality. Lift against the quotient by hT_i to prove divisibility. T_i is regular on A[T] and remains so by flatness of the framing; h is regular on power series, even when A has zero divisors.

targets.name: QWitt.framedJacksonDerivative
targets.statement: Under 8.2 define the continuous A[[h]]-linear operator D_i by hT_i D_i(f)=γ_i(f)−f. These operators commute, satisfy D_i(fg)=fD_i(g)+γ_i(g)D_i(f), and D_i(T_i^n)=[n]_q T_i^(n−1) for n≥1, D_i(T_j)=0 for j≠i. Reduction modulo h is the coordinate derivation ∂/∂T_i on R.
hypotheses: The framing and regularity assumptions of 8.2; n≥1.

locator.where: §§4.7–4.8, lines 2842–2872; scholze §3, scholze lines 291–304; printed wagner v5 p. 57; scholze v1 p. 6

api.name: framedJacksonDerivative_unique
api.statement: The equation hT_iD_i=γ_i−id uniquely determines D_i.

api.name: framedJacksonDerivative_commute
api.statement: D_iD_j=D_jD_i and D_iγ_j=γ_jD_i for i≠j.

api.name: framedJacksonDerivative_map
api.statement: Framing-compatible maps intertwine D_i.

tests.name: QWitt.framedJacksonDerivative_1
tests.statement: D(T²)=(1+q)T and D(T³)=(1+q+q²)T²; an ordinary derivative would give 2T and 3T².

tests.name: QWitt.framedJacksonDerivative_2

targets.name: QWitt.framedTwoTermCohomology
targets.statement: Let S_α=ℤ_p[[h]]/(q^(p^α)−1), q=1+h. For 0≤e≤α, let K_{α,e} be S_α→S_α in degrees 0,1 with differential q^(p^e)−1. Its H⁰ is [p^(α−e)]_{q^(p^e)}S_α≅ℤ_p[[h]]/(q^(p^e)−1), and H¹ is that same quotient. If e₁≥e₂, the ordinary tensor complex K_{α,e₁}⊗_{S_α}K_{α,e₂} is K_{α,e₂}⊕K_{α,e₂}[−1]. Thus every summand of 9.2 has p-torsion-free cohomology, and so does H*(H□^∧_p/(q^(p^α)−1)).
hypotheses: p prime; α≥0; 0≤e_i≤α; H□ has the hypotheses of 9.2; rank zero handled separately.

targets.name: QWitt.framedBockstein
targets.statement: For a perfectly covered Λ-ring A and étale framing with finitely many coordinates □ of R/A, put f_m=q^m−1 and E_m=H*(H□/f_m). Since f_m is injective in every term of H□, specialize the generic DGA Bockstein to β_m:E_m^i→E_m^(i+1), with β_m([x])=[d_H(x)/f_m]. It is independent of the cycle lift, squares to zero and is a degree-one derivation. For d|m the reduction F and multiplication V=[m/d]_{q^d} satisfy Fβ_mV=β_d.
hypotheses: A perfectly covered; R has a specified étale framing with finitely many coordinates; m,d>0 and d divides m.

Apply the generic Bockstein supplier to H□ and f_m. Its cycle-lift equation fixes the sign, and its change-of-parameter identity for f_d dividing f_m gives Fβ_mV=β_d. This specializes the generic theorem rather than constructing a second DGA Bockstein theory.

targets.name: QWitt.framedCohomologySystem

Give it its canonical Q_m(R/A)→E_m⁰ map, F_{m/d} induced by quotient reduction and V_{m/d} induced by multiplication [m/d]_{q^d}. This is a differential q-FV system. Its canonical Q_mΩ*→E_m map is induced by initiality.

targets.proofSketch: Construct the degree-zero map by the finite arithmetic fracture square, using the polynomial comparison and the framed p-adic lifts on each completed factor. Lemma 4.25 is the cohomology/completion supplier gap. Reduce ℤ-torsion-freeness to 9.3 by finite-type and flat étale base change; commutativity follows because γ_i−id vanishes on cocycles modulo q^m−1. Torsion-freeness forces odd squares to zero, including at 2, and proves the Teichmüller relation. All constructions remain dependent on the specified frame.

targets.name: QWitt.primePowerSmoothInduction
targets.statement: For a perfectly covered A and every prime p, establish simultaneously for all α≥0: (a) Q_{p^α}Ω*_{R/A} is degreewise p-torsion-free for smooth R/A; (b) for framed R the canonical map (Q_{p^α}Ω*)^∧_p→H*(H□^∧_p/(q^(p^α)−1)), with Bockstein differential, is an isomorphism; (c) for framed R there is an explicit quasi-isomorphism (Ω*_{R/A}⊗_{A,ψ_{p^α}}A[q]/(q^(p^α)−1))^∧_p→(Q_{p^α}Ω*)^∧_p induced in degree zero by s_{p^α/A} of the coordinate Frobenius lift; (d) for polynomial R and dξ≡0 mod p at level p^α, ξ=F_p(ω)+pη for some ω at level p^(α+1) and η at level p^α, in the same form degree.
hypotheses: A perfectly covered; p any prime including 2; α≥0; R smooth, framed or polynomial as specified separately in (a)–(d). Statement (c) is an equivalence of complexes, not a degreewise isomorphism.

api.statement: The induction proceeds (d at α−1)⇒(a at α)⇒(b at α)⇒(c at α)⇒(d at α).

api.name: QWitt.primePowerSmoothInduction_base
api.statement: At α=0 use Ω*_{R/A}, the h-Bockstein identity and the polynomial Cartier cycle decomposition; the α=−1 premise is empty.

targets.proofSketch: Treat (a)–(d) as one simultaneous induction, not four circular prerequisites. For (a), use the first-ghost quotient and (d at α−1) to kill a putative p-torsion form; extend from polynomial to smooth by 7.7. For (b), compare the short exact sequences with kernel im V_p+im dV_p using 9.3 and the zero-index Frobenius summand. For (c), use the prismatic Frobenius/décalage comparison gap with the explicit C□ map in 8.5, then identify it through (b). For (d), decompose polynomial de Rham cycles modulo p into Cartier monomials and exact forms; Teichmüller identities and FdV=d lift both. The functorial comparison of §9.7 extends this framed milestone by PD presentations and étale descent.

targets.name: QWitt.smoothDeRhamComparison
targets.statement: For a perfectly covered arithmetic Λ-ring A, every smooth A-algebra R, every prime p and every positive integer m=p^αn with α≥0 and gcd(n,p)=1, construct a natural equivalence of p-complete E∞-A[q]-algebras ∏_{d|n}(Ω*_{R/A}⊗ᴸ_{A,ψ_{p^αd}}A[q]/Φ_d(q^(p^α)))^∧_p ≃ (Q_mΩ*_{R/A})^∧_p. The tensor is derived and uses ψ_{p^αd} on the right A-factor; Ω* denotes the ordinary de Rham algebra viewed in the enhanced derived category. The equivalence is functorial for every A-algebra map between smooth A-algebras, without a framing choice.
hypotheses: A perfectly covered; R smooth over A; p any prime, including 2; m>0; α=v_p(m); n=m/p^α; gcd(n,p)=1. No Noetherian, perfectness or global framing hypothesis is imposed on R.

api.statement: Every A-algebra map R→S between smooth A-algebras gives a commuting square of equivalences in the ∞-category of p-complete E∞-A[q]-algebras, coherently with identities and composition.

api.name: QWitt.differential_pLocalDecomposition
api.statement: For every A-algebra R and m=p^αn with gcd(n,p)=1, put C_α=A[q]/(q^(p^α)−1). Then (Q_mΩ*)_(p) ≅ ∏_{d|n}(Q_{p^α}Ω*⊗_{C_α,σ_d}A_(p)[q]/Φ_d(q^(p^α))) as DG A_(p)[q]-algebras, where σ_d(a)=ψ_d(a) and σ_d(q)=q^d. For perfectly covered A these maps out of C_α are flat, so the ordinary tensors agree with derived tensors over C_α.

For A=R=ℤ their product is ℤ_3[q]/(q²−1) by Chinese remainders; at p=2 the two factors are not comaximal, so m=2 instead has the single prime-power factor q²−1. In the intermediate decomposition use derived tensor over C_α: for n=1,A=R=ℤ, replacing it by tensor over ℤ[q] with C_α produces the extra Tor₁=C_α, since q^(p^α)−1 is regular in ℤ[q].

targets.proofSketch: For a prime power choose a surjection P→R̂_p with P p-completely ind-smooth over Â_p and carrying a compatible δ-structure. Use its δ-compatible PD envelope D(P→R̂_p), the PD de Rham complex and its multiplicative crystalline Poincaré equivalence to (Ω*_{R/A})^∧_p. The relative comparison of §4.6 induces a map from the PD de Rham complex after killing p-primary torsion on the q-Witt side. Section 9.6(a) allows descent to Q_{p^α}Ω*. Compare different presentations via their completed tensor coproducts: the presentation category is weakly contractible, and a functorial free δ-presentation gives coherent naturality. On an étale frame this map is §9.6(c), so §7.7 and ordinary de Rham étale descent prove equivalence for arbitrary smooth R. For general m, construct the displayed p-local product by the differential q-FV universal property, as in §3.7; flat Adams twists and cyclotomic scalar maps identify ordinary and derived tensors over C_α=A[q]/(q^(p^α)−1). Apply the prime-power comparison to its factors and p-complete.

gaps.title: Cyclotomic integer ideals and completion topology
gaps.detail: Beyond the Mathlib polynomial and factorization declarations above, require: for m>1 the ideal generated by [p]_{q^(m/p)} for p|m is (Φ_m); distinct cyclotomic factors meet only at a prime-power ratio, with the stated characteristic-p quotient; p-local factorization and Chinese remainders; √(p,Φ_d)=√(p,Φ_{pd}) for every d>0, including p|d. Equality of completion functors is by radical, not equality of these ideals. Do not apply the prime-generator formula at m=1 or the distinct-factor formula at equal indices. (wagner v5 §§2.1–2.3, pp. 8–23, wagner lines 305–1190; wagner-habiro v2 §2.7, pp. 15–16, wagner-habiro lines 647–661).

gaps.title: Unbounded cochain completion under degreewise torsion bounds
gaps.detail: For an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, cochain complex M of ℤ[q]-modules and a prime p, if each term and H^i(M) has bounded h-power torsion and is p-torsion-free, and each corresponding reduction modulo p has bounded h-power torsion, then degreewise ordinary h-completion represents derived completion, preserves these conditions, and H^i commutes with h- and (p,h)-completion, for h=q−1. This is Wagner Lemma 4.25, v5 pp. 64–65, wagner lines 3198–3227; bounds may depend on the degree. Required extension: DerivedModuleAlgebra, Part II.

gaps.title: Generic multiplicative Bockstein extension
gaps.detail: Required for an associative cochain DGA P over a commutative B and central degree-zero f regular in every term: β_f on H*(P/f), computed by dx=fy, is independent of lifts, satisfies β_f²=0 and the signed Leibniz rule, is natural, and obeys Fβ_fV=β_g for g|f with F reduction and V multiplication by f/g when both scalars are termwise regular. The maps F and V in this last identity are graded additive maps; F is multiplicative. Source: wagner v5 pp. 61, 64, wagner lines 3026–3032 and 3178–3194, with the cycle-lift proof. The pinned group-cohomology Bocksteins have different carriers and codomains.

gaps.title: Differential-ideal quotients of associative DG algebras
gaps.needs: Required extension of DGAInfinity Layer 1: differential-ideal quotients.
gaps.detail: For an associative cochain B-DGA P over a commutative ring B and a homogeneous two-sided ideal J with d(J)⊆J, construct the degreewise quotient DGA P/J and projection. DGA maps P/J→E correspond to DGA maps P→E killing J. The quotient retains graded commutativity and strict odd alternation when P has these properties. A generated differential ideal is the least differential two-sided graded ideal containing the specified homogeneous relations. This interface concerns algebra ideals. (wagner v5 Proposition 3.12 and Definition 3.13, pp. 40–41, wagner lines 1956–2010, using the differential-ideal quotient universal property).
